title: Proactive model prober with kernel-signature-guided fallback plan for speculative decoding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We frequently need sub-50ms tail latency for short response workloads. Traditional speculative decode implementations pick candidate models based on static priorities or coarse heuristics and rely on full prefill probes, which increases cost and stalls in the presence of kernel mismatches (e.g., model layout, quantization, sequence length).

Goal: Implement a lightweight proactive model prober that issues micro-prefill probes, computes a small 'kernel signature' fingerprint, and uses that to score candidate model variants in real-time. Combine the prober output with an acceptance curve estimator so the orchestrator can choose a fast candidate and have an automated, graceful fallback if acceptance confidence is low.

Proposed approach:
1) Micro-probing: emit a short, single-token prefill probe to 1-2 candidate models in parallel to collect early latency and KV-cache behavior without doing a full prefill. Probe size is configurable (default 1 token).
2) Kernel signature: compute a compact fingerprint from probe metadata: measured kernel invocation latency distribution, observed allocation pattern, and returned prefill token logits summary. The signature is a short vector stored in the request context and in the runtime trace.
3) Candidate scoring: maintain an LRU per-route small table of historical (kernel_signature -> acceptance_rate) metrics for model variants and hardware profiles. Score candidates by combining current probe signature similarity, model quality prior, and cost weight.
4) Acceptance estimator: run a lightweight logistic model (pretrained offline) that outputs acceptance probability given score and request-level covariates (prompt length, route SLO, user tier). Acceptance thresholds are configurable by SLO.
5) Fast-failover: if speculative decode result fails acceptance (below threshold) or the probe shows kernel mismatch, immediately cancel decode stream and reissue to fallback model variant (stateful rollback plan reuses cached KV where possible).
6) Observability: emit acceptance probabilities, probe signatures, probe latencies, and fallback counts to Console with a new per-route dashboard.

Why this is different: we avoid expensive full prefill probes and instead synthesize a runtime-driven kernel fingerprint to make model-selection decisions that are sensitive to both software kernel and hardware behavior. This reduces unnecessary full-prefill cost while preserving tail latency SLOs via fast fallback.

Risks and mitigations:
- Probe overhead: probes could increase per-request work; mitigate by limiting probes to small fraction (canary first) and using adaptive sampling.
- False acceptance/regression: acceptance estimator may be miscalibrated; mitigate with A/B evaluation and gradual rollout with eval prompt sets.
- Complexity in state rollback: ensure we only fast-fallback when rollback safely reuses KV cache or when state is ephemeral; add explicit invariants in orchestrator.

Success metrics (before GA):
- 20% reduction in average tokens processed by failed speculates vs baseline (measured on benchmark workload).
- No >2% regression in model-quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-quality signal depending on op) during canary.
- Tail latency (p95 for short prompts) improvement of >=10% on routes where spec probing is enabled.

Compatibility: integrates with runtime kernel profiler and Console tracing. Requires a small runtime extension to emit probe-level metadata and a cache table in the router service.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits kernel_signature and probe metrics for probed requests
Orchestrator selects candidates using probe-informed scoring with configurable threshold
Fast-failover cancels speculative decode and successfully routes to fallback within configured timeout
Console dashboard shows per-route probe acceptance, fallback rate, and cost delta
Automated canary rollout gates ensure <2% model-quality regression on evaluation set
